explain.say: Tardigrades, or water bears, are eight-legged animals about half a millimetre long. They live in films of water on moss, lichen and soil, so their home often dries out.

faq.a: A tun is the dried-up, barrel-shaped form a tardigrade takes when its home dries out. It pulls in its legs and loses almost all its water, then can wait years until water returns.
asks: What happens when a tardigrade dries out?

faq.q: How do tardigrades protect their cells when dry?
faq.a: They make special proteins that turn into a glassy gel as the cells dry, holding delicate cell parts in place. One protein, called Dsup, also helps protect their DNA from radiation damage.
asks: Why don't tardigrade cells break when dry?

faq.a: Cryptobiosis means hidden life. It is a state where an animal's metabolism slows so much it is almost undetectable, yet it can come back to life later. Tardigrades enter it when dried or frozen.

faq.q: How do tardigrades survive in space?
faq.a: In 2007, dried tardigrades spent ten days outside a spacecraft in orbit. Many survived the vacuum and cold, and some even survived the harsh radiation, then revived and had babies back on Earth.
No. Active, wet tardigrades are fairly delicate, and even tuns die with long exposure to high heat. They survive extremes they would never meet in nature, but only for limited times.

facts: In 2007, dried tardigrades survived ten days exposed to space in low Earth orbit on the FOTON-M3 mission.
Tardigrades revived from a moss sample frozen in Antarctica for over 30 years were reported in 2016.
